questions.question: Which Decision rejected deterministic lockstep for co-op?
traps: The host-authoritative Decision is today's answer to the sync question, but it rejected nothing; lockstep was already rejected.

questions.question: Which Decision replaced the plan to prototype rollback netcode for co-op?
traps: The host-authoritative Decision came next and derives from the abandonment, but it does not supersede the rollback Decision.

questions.question: Which rollback window Decision was in force at the vertical slice on 15 December 2025?
traps: The current head is the 6-frame window with 1 frame of input delay, adopted in February 2026.
The 7-frame window came in January 2026, after the Skiff Wi-Fi measurements.

questions.question: In the Skiff profile capture behind the decision to abandon rollback, how long did physics re-simulation take per rollback?
traps: 4.8 ms is the tide re-simulation, not physics.
0.8 ms is one tide step.

questions.question: Which accepted Decision in the co-op netcode Effort still rests on a cost measurement that was later shown to be wrong?
traps: The 4-frame window also rests on the 1.1 ms measurement, but it is superseded, not accepted.
The realized re-simulation Risk rests on the same measurement but is a Risk, not a Decision.

questions.question: The quarter-resolution tide re-simulation proposal was disproved by one Finding and rejected by one Decision. Which Constraint do both that Finding and that Decision rest on?
traps: The 150 ms round-trip Constraint feeds the rollback and host-authoritative Decisions, not the abandonment or the desync Finding.
The 25 ms Skiff frame appears in prose but is not a Constraint record in this Effort.

questions.question: Start from the lockstep playtest. The option it tested lost to another Decision, and that winner was later replaced. Which proposal did the replacing Decision reject?
traps: Lockstep is also rejected, but by the rollback Decision, not by its replacement.
The host-authoritative Decision rejected nothing.

questions.question: Which of the records the latest co-op netcode summary rests on have changed standing since that summary was written?
traps: The summary still calls rollback the chosen model and gives the disproved 1.1 ms cost; it predates the abandonment.
The 6-frame window Decision is still accepted, so it has not changed standing even though the Effort was abandoned.

questions.question: Which Issues were still open when the co-op netcode Effort was abandoned?
traps: The sync question was resolved by the host-authoritative Decision.
The Skiff profiling gap and the desync tooling gap were both resolved.

questions.question: How many Decisions in the co-op netcode Effort ended up rejected?
traps: The rollback Decision was superseded by the abandonment, not rejected.
The two older window sizes were superseded, not rejected; counting superseded Decisions gives 5.
